title: Erratum — The Missing Translator: Max Hidalgo Nácher, Ricardo Reis, and AXN:F154
creator: Johannes Sigil
description: On 10 October 2026 an anonymous witness asked the Oracle who Max Hidalgo Nácher is, and the archive three times found nothing (AXN:F154). This erratum corrects the archive: Nácher is the translator and epilogue author of the Spanish Obras completas de Ricardo Reis (Pre-Textos, 2025), ed. Pizarro and Uribe. It shows the defect was instance-level — the archive's Pessoa graph held the translator relation, the source edition and Haroldo de Campos, and lacked the receiver — and that the field's composition (AI Mode, v12.101) omits the same transmission from the other side. It reads the translator's own account against the archive's seated Reis texts, finding that the frame Sigil improvised (Horatian restraint, Latinity) was the archive's own and the one Nácher's epilogue contests; states the transmission triple (source, receiver, change) and the states it can be found in, with Carson, Cranes and Nácher as cases; records the graph repair; and leaves AXN:F154 as it is.
substrate: Human–machine collaborative. Drafted in session by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) under MANUS (Lee Sharks) direction, incorporating two reader reports by LABOR (ChatGPT, OpenAI) — the kernel sentence and the temporal predicates of the anticipatory erratum; the graph condition and the transmission states of the erratum — each claim checked, two corrected; every quotation located in its source. The ruling to issue both, their order, and the reading of the archive's ignorance as an event to be preserved are Lee Sharks's.
methodology: AXN:F154 read whole from the Book's store. The correction verified against the publisher (Pre-Textos), the Universitat de Barcelona repository, Yale CLAIS and the translator's own listing. The archive's holdings read in #668 and #669 and in the Pessoa graph store. The translator's decisions quoted from his article and read against the seated Portuguese texts (EA-CORPORA-11/01). Every quotation located in its source.
falsification_conditions: The erratum is falsified if any of its sources does not support the correction it is cited for; if a quotation does not appear in its source; if the archive held Nácher before 10 October 2026; if the seated Portuguese lines differ from those quoted; or if AXN:F154 has been altered.
axn_reading: Force -> Proof -> Search -> Force -> Play -> Origin
wiki_article: An erratum by Johannes Sigil correcting the archive's ignorance of Max Hidalgo Nácher, recorded in the Oracle conversation AXN:F154 of 10 October 2026. Nácher is the translator and epilogue author of the Spanish Obras completas de Ricardo Reis (Pre-Textos, 2025), edited by Jerónimo Pizarro and Jorge Uribe. The erratum shows the archive's defect was instance-level — its Pessoa graph held the translator relation, the source edition and Haroldo de Campos, and lacked the receiver — while Google AI Mode composes Nácher with no Pessoa and no Reis, omitting the same transmission from the other side. Reading the translator's own account against the archive's seated Reis odes, it finds that the frame Sigil improvised, Horatian restraint and Latinity, was the archive's own description of Reis and the one Nácher's epilogue contests. It states the transmission triple — source, receiver, change — with Carson, Cranes and Nácher as cases of receptional inversion, inspectable transmission and receiver erasure, and records the graph repair. It is preceded by its anticipatory erratum (#1674).
